findings.description:
It is possible to execute code on the remote host through Samba.

The version of the Samba server installed on the remote host is affected by multiple heap
                    overflow vulnerabilities, which can be exploited remotely to execute code with the privileges of the
                    Samba daemon.
findings.mitigation: Upgrade to Samba version 3.0.25 or later.
findings.title: Samba NDR MS-RPC Request Heap-Based Remote Buffer Overflow

findings.description:
It is possible to access a network share.

The remote has one or more Windows shares that can be accessed through the network with the
                    given credentials.

                    Depending on the share rights, it may allow an attacker to read/write confidential data.
findings.mitigation:
To restrict access under Windows, open Explorer, do a right click on each share, go to the
                    'sharing' tab, and click on 'permissions'.
findings.title: Microsoft Windows SMB Shares Unprivileged Access

findings.description:
It is possible to obtain information about the remote host.

The remote service understands the Bonjour (also known as ZeroConf or mDNS) protocol, which
                    allows anyone to uncover information from the remote host such as its operating system type and
                    exact version, its hostname, and the list of services it is running.

                    This plugin attempts to discover mDNS used by hosts that are not on the network segment on which
                    Nessus resides.
findings.mitigation: Filter incoming traffic to UDP port 5353, if desired.
findings.title: mDNS Detection (Remote Network)

findings.description:
The remote service could be identified.

It was possible to identify the remote service by its banner or by looking at the error
                    message it sends when it receives an HTTP request.
findings.title: Service Detection

findings.description:
It is possible to determine the exact time set on the remote host.

The remote host answers to an ICMP timestamp request. This allows an attacker to know the
                    date that is set on the targeted machine, which may assist an unauthenticated, remote attacker in
                    defeating time-based authentication protocols.

                    Timestamps returned from machines running Windows Vista / 7 / 2008 / 2008 R2 are deliberately
                    incorrect, but usually within 1000 seconds of the actual system time.
findings.mitigation: Filter out the ICMP timestamp requests (13), and the outgoing ICMP timestamp replies (14).
findings.title: ICMP Timestamp Request Remote Date Disclosure

findings.description:
It is possible to obtain the version number of the remote DNS server.

The remote host is running BIND or another DNS server that reports its version number when
                    it receives a special request for the text 'version.bind' in the domain 'chaos'.

                    This version is not necessarily accurate and could even be forged, as some DNS servers send the
                    information based on a configuration file.
findings.mitigation:
It is possible to hide the version number of BIND by using the 'version' directive
                    in the 'options' section in named.conf.
findings.title: DNS Server BIND version Directive Remote Version Detection

findings.description:
The DNS server discloses the remote host name.

It is possible to learn the remote host name by querying the remote DNS server for 'hostname.bind'
                    in the CHAOS domain.
findings.mitigation:
It may be possible to disable this feature. Consult the vendor's documentation for more
                    information.
findings.title: DNS Server hostname.bind Map Hostname Disclosure

findings.description:
It is possible to determine which TCP ports are open.

This plugin is a SYN 'half-open' port scanner. It shall be reasonably quick even
                    against a firewalled target.

                    Note that SYN scans are less intrusive than TCP (full connect) scans against broken services, but
                    they might cause problems for less robust firewalls and also leave unclosed connections on the
                    remote target, if the network is loaded.
findings.mitigation: Protect your target with an IP filter.
findings.title: Nessus SYN scanner

findings.description:
A DNS server is listening on the remote host.

The remote service is a Domain Name System (DNS) server, which provides a mapping between
                    hostnames and IP addresses.
findings.mitigation:
Disable this service if it is not needed or restrict access to internal hosts only if the
                    service is available externally.
findings.title: DNS Server Detection

findings.description:
The remote service implements TCP timestamps.

The remote host implements TCP timestamps, as defined by RFC1323. A side effect of this
                    feature is that the uptime of the remote host can sometimes be computed.
findings.title: TCP/IP Timestamps Supported

findings.description:
It was possible to obtain traceroute information.

Makes a traceroute to the remote host.
findings.title: Traceroute Information

findings.description:
It is possible to obtain network information.

It was possible to obtain the browse list of the remote Windows system by sending a request
                    to the LANMAN pipe. The browse list is the list of the nearest Windows systems of the remote host.
findings.title: Microsoft Windows SMB LanMan Pipe Server Listing Disclosure
